subject: HydroCore committed capacity: tokens/sec sizing, latency SLO fit and headroom
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@hydrocore.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis@hydrocore.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask: committed plan + p95 fit

Hi Karthik,

Quick context: HydroCore is preparing the Q3 committed capacity order and we need Redwood to confirm how the committed GPU pool maps to our performance SLOs. High level workload: interactive assistants + long-form summarization. Key constraints:

- Target external SLO: p95 token latency <= 250ms for interactive routes (short requests); 95th percentile for batch summarization acceptable up to 800ms.
- Traffic pattern: normal day 1.6M tokens/day; predictable daily surge 14:00-14:30 PDT with ~80 req/s (peak) for the assistant route. Average request lengths: interactive 140 tokens, summarization 1,200 tokens (but low qps).
- Models we want to serve: a 13B optimized variant for interactive, and a 70B quantized variant for high-quality summarization. Routing policy would prefer 13B for cost-critical flows and only route to 70B when quality required.

Attached: hydrocore_estimate_v3.xlsx (usage forecast), plus sample latency traces. Can you:
1) Map peak tokens/sec to GPUs needed for each model variant (give tokens/sec/GPU assumptions).
2) Show headroom % to meet p95 targets under 10/30/50% surge scenarios.
3) Propose a minimal committed slab (and burst policy) that keeps costs predictable but meets SLOs.

Thanks — need this for the procurement call on Thu.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform — HydroCore
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hydrocore.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: committed plan + p95 fit

Samira — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. I ran a quick sizing pass and attached a working sheet (hydrocore_estimate_v3.xlsx) with line-by-line math. Summary below — call out that these are conservative, measured estimates using our A100-80GB serving profile and baseline kernel stack.

Executive summary (short):
- Peak tokens/sec calculation (assistant route): 80 req/s * 140 tokens = 11,200 tokens/sec peak.
- Sustained daily average across both routes: ~19 tokens/sec (from your 1.6M/day), but bursts drive capacity planning.

Throughput assumptions (tokens/sec per GPU, single-tenant Dedicated A100 80GB):
- 13B quantized (q4-like): ~2,300 tokens/sec per GPU (conservative for p95-stable latency).
- 70B quantized (int8 path): ~480 tokens/sec per GPU (higher variance on tail).

Sizing math (peak, interactive route):
- 11,200 tokens/sec peak / 2,300 tokens/sec per GPU => ~4.9 GPUs => round up to 6 GPUs for placement/packing overhead and to keep queuing low.

Sizing math (summarization route when routed to 70B):
- Summarization concurrent profile is low (expected <5 concurrency), but a single 70B GPU handles ~480 tokens/sec => a 1–2 GPU footprint depending on batching (recommend 2 GPUs to avoid queueing spikes).

Headroom scenarios (for interactive route, baseline 6 GPUs):
- +10% surge: headroom OK (~0.9 spare GPUs equivalent).
- +30% surge: effective need ~8 GPUs.
- +50% surge: effective need ~9–10 GPUs and latency risk at p95.

Recommendation (committed slab & burst):
- Commit 8 GPUs (Dedicated pool) for predictable throughput.
- Configure burst/buffer policy: allow 4 additional burst GPUs from shared capacity for short windows (throttled by priority), with automatic fallback to 13B smaller model variants when burst budget exhausted.
- Maintain a 25% safety buffer in token budget for unexpected tail behavior; this is encoded in the attached workbook.

Notes about latency and tail behavior:
- 70B quantized path shows higher p95 variance in our tests; if HydroCore requires strict p95 parity, prefer serving long-form via a 13B+context hybrid (chunking + merge) to reduce tail latency.
- We recommend a 2-week perf canary where we capture p50/p95/p99 and token-cost; will use that as trigger for final commit adjustments.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm willingness to commit 8 GPUs + 4 burst and we’ll convert to a formal offer.
2) Ben — can you review pricing impact if we move to 30% headroom?
3) Schedule a 60-minute perf canary window Wed/Thu with HydroCore traffic replay.

Attached the p95-latency-plot.png showing our internal runs and the workbook with calculations.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@hydrocore.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: committed plan + p95 fit

Looping in pricing/ops note — agree with Karthik's conservative throughput numbers. A couple of quick asks from our side:

- Given this is an enterprise commitment, recommend we plan for 30% safety buffer (not 25%) on the committed slab to keep SLOs tight during early adoption. That moves committed slab recommendation from 8 -> 10 GPUs.
- For the burst policy, suggest a hard cap on burst minutes per day (e.g., 30 minutes of unlimited burst) to protect other tenants. We can translate that into a price-break for HydroCore.

If HydroCore is price-sensitive, we can offer a phased commit: 8 GPUs initial commit + option to top up to 10 after the canary if p95 looks good. That reduces upfront spend and gives empirical data.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@hydrocore.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: committed plan + p95 fit

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A couple of clarifying Qs from procurement and infra: 

1) For the interactive route, if we commit 8 GPUs + 4 burst, and we see a 30% extra unexpected surge for 45 minutes, how will Redwood prioritize requests? Will it fall back to 13B routing and what is the expected p95 impact when fallback occurs?
2) For summarization (70B), is the 2 GPU recommendation enough to keep p95 <800ms if we batch at 2–4 concurrent summaries?

We prefer the phased commit approach — start at 8 and then expand to 10 after the canary if metrics look stable. Can you provide the exact playbook steps and monitoring hooks so our SREs can sign off?

Samira
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hydrocore.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: committed plan + p95 fit

Samira — great, phased commit accepted. Quick answers and action items below.

1) Prioritization / fallback behavior:
- During burst > committed+burst capacity, routing will: 1) prefer queued requests for interactive 13B until queue threshold, 2) route lower-priority/less-latency-sensitive work to the quantized 13B, and 3) if still overloaded, apply a graceful degradation policy (reduce max response tokens + notify client) to keep p95 within reason.
- Expected p95 impact on interactive route when falling back from local 13B to smaller 13B-optimized: median increases negligibly (~10–20ms), p95 could climb by ~40–90ms depending on request length. That keeps you within 250–300ms in most cases; we'll capture exact delta during canary.

2) Summarization (70B) guidance:
- For summarization batched at 2–4 concurrent jobs, 2 x 70B GPUs is our safe minimum. Expected p95 is ~600–750ms under the batching profile in your workbook. If HydroCore wants a tighter p95 (<600ms) for long summaries, we should either increase to 3 GPUs or convert to a chunked 13B+merge strategy.

Canary & runbook (high level):
- Duration: 14 days with a first 48-hour intensive traffic replay.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies per route, tokens/sec served, queue depth, GPU occupancy, KV cache hit rates. Dashboards will be shared (we'll add HydroCore SREs to Redwood Console).
- Triggers: if p95 > 300ms consistently during peak windows for >2 hours, we auto-trigger a top-up recommendation.
- DOCS/links: runbook-deltas.pdf attached (contains escalation steps, rollback commands, and monitoring alerts).

Concrete proposal:
- Phase 1 (commit): 8 GPUs Dedicated + 4 GPU burst pool (30m/day hard cap); 30% safety buffer set as target for initial two weeks.
- Phase 2 (after canary): top-up to 10 GPUs if measured p95 shows risk or if traffic growth exceeds projections.

Action items:
- Karthik to schedule Wed 06/06 10:00–12:00 PDT for traffic replay with HydroCore.
- Ben to draft phased pricing term and burst cap language for procurement.
- Lauren to provision initial Dedicated slab and Console dashboard access for HydroCore SREs.

I'll follow up with a compact one-page PDF that summarizes numbers for procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: hydrocore_estimate_v3.xlsx, p95-latency-plot.png, runbook-deltas.pdf
